chunks: As for what was narrated — Muhammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Haytham ibn Abī Masrūq al-Nahdī, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Samāʿa, who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): 'I urinate, then wipe myself with stones, and after my istibra' moisture comes from me that soils my trousers.' He said: 'There is no harm in it.'

This does not contradict what we have stated — that urine must necessarily be washed — for two reasons. The first: it is possible this was specific to a situation in which [the questioner] could not find water, and it was thus permissible for him at that point to suffice with stones.

The second [reason]: the report does not state that he said salat was permissible with that even without washing it. He only said there was no harm in that moisture which comes out after istibra' — and that is correct. Furthermore, it is possible that the moisture which came out after istibra' was wadiy, for that is what typically occurs in such a case, and wadiy does not invalidate wudu according to us [Shia jurists].

Then he [the jurist], may Allah the Exalted support him, said: 'Whoever urinates must wash only the exit point of urine and nothing else. Likewise, the junub washes his male organ, and a separate istinja' is not required of him, because washing the exterior of his entire body covers every part that water reaches.' This [hadith] indicates that.

key_terms.اسْتِبَاحَةُ: istibahah — rendering an act legally permissible (here: unlocking the permissibility of salat)
key_terms.اسْتِبْرَائِي: istibra' — post-urination procedure ensuring complete expulsion of residual urine
key_terms.الِاقْتِصَارُ: sufficing with stones as substitute when water is unavailable
key_terms.الْوَدْيَ: wadiy — white viscous fluid discharged after urination; does not break wudu

ai.seo_question: Does moisture after istibra' require washing, and what does Imam al-Kazim (AS) rule in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: Sama'a narrates asking Imam Abu al-Hasan Musa al-Kazim (AS) about moisture that appears after istibra', and the Imam declares it is of no concern. Sheikh al-Tusi reconciles this with the ruling that urine must be washed via two jurisprudential arguments, noting further that the moisture may be wadiy — a bodily fluid which does not break wudu according to Shia fiqh — before concluding that only the urinary exit point requires washing.
